questions.question:
**Direction: Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.**

Don't sound so **__excited__**.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"eager."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Excited"** means feeling or showing enthusiasm and eagerness. (उत्साह और उत्सुकता महसूस करना या दिखाना)

 
 
• **Example**: *I am very **excited**__ for tomorrow.*
 
 
 
• **"Eager"** means having or showing keen interest or intense desire for something. (किसी चीज़ के प्रति गहरी रुचि या तीव्र इच्छा होना या प्रदर्शित होना)
 __
 
• **Example**: *The man was **eager**__ to please me.*
 
 
 
• Synonym of **excited** is **eager**.
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 -** casual**: Relaxed and unconcerned; not showing much interest or care. (निश्चिंत और बेपरवाह; ज्यादा दिलचस्पी या परवाह नहीं दिखाना)
 
• Option 2 - **composed**: Calm and in control of one's emotions; not easily agitated or disturbed. (शांत और अपनी भावनाओं पर नियंत्रण रखना; आसानी से उत्तेजित या परेशान नहीं होना)
 
• Option 4 - **tired**: Feeling or showing the need for sleep or rest; lacking in energy or enthusiasm. (नींद या आराम की आवश्यकता महसूस करना या दिखाना; ऊर्जा या उत्साह की कमी)

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the appropriate synonym for the underlined word.**

You look around and you see green, **__happy__** plants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"blissful."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Happy" **means feeling or showing pleasure; pleased. (आनंद का अनुभव करने या उसे व्‍यक्त करने वाला; प्रसन्‍न, प्रफुल्‍ल)

 
 
• **Example**: *She is very happy.*
 
 
 
• Synonyms of **happy **include ecstatic, blissful, elated, and euphoric.
 
• **"Blissful"** means extremely happy or joyful. (सुखद, आनंदमय, चरम सुख)
 
 
• **Example**: *After receiving the good news, she felt **blissful**__ and couldn't stop smiling.*
 
 
 
• The correct answer is Option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 (**mourning)** means feeling or expressing sorrow or grief, usually due to a loss. (शोकमग्‍न, दुखी)
 
• Option 2 (**nascent**) means just beginning to exist or develop. (आरंभिक अवस्था, उदीयमान; विकासशील)
 
• Option 4 (**gloomy**) means dark or dim, often used to describe a sad or depressing atmosphere. (ऐसा गहरा कि उदास कर दे)

Although people had been on watch and / the watchkeepers were very, very tired, / everyone were up and buzzing.

the watchkeepers were very, very tired,

questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is **"everyone were up and buzzing."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject **"everyone"** is singular, but the verb **"were"** is incorrect as it is the past tense of **"be"** and should be replaced with** "was" **to agree with the singular** "everyone."**
 
• **“Everyone”** is treated as singular pronoun, so it's always used with a singular verb form.
 
 
• **Example: *****Everyone is**__ responsible for this failure.*
 
 
 
• The correct sentence would be *"Although people had been on watch and the watchkeepers were very, very tired, __**everyone was up and buzzing**__."*
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

questions.question:

Your body will respond by/ getting more muscular and/ strong before you know it.
questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is** "strong before you know it."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the part **"strong before you know it" **of the sentence.
 
• In this sentence, we can see the use of **"more muscular"** which is a comparative degree.
 
• So, to maintain the uniformity, we have to write **"strong"** in comparative degree.
 
• The comparative form of the adjective** 'strong'** is **'stronger.'**
 
• The correct answer is Option 1.

 

**Correct sentence**: *Your body will respond by getting more muscular and **stronger before you know it**__.*

**Direction: Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.**

He lost his temper (**by a driver**) flashed her headlights as he overtook.
questions.solution:

__
 
• The original sentence is grammatically incorrect because** "by a driver"** is not a correct prepositional phrase to use in this context.
 
• The preposition "after" means later than something; at a later time. (पश्‍चात; बाद में)
 
 
• **Example**: *He came **after**__ the train left.*
 
 
 
• The correct preposition to use in this context is **"after",** which indicates that the driver flashing her headlights caused the speaker to lose his temper.
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

 

**Correct sentence**: *He lost his temper __**after a driver**__ flashed her headlights as he overtook.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "Afterwards"** means at a later time. (बाद में, पश्‍चात)
 
• **Option 3: "Considering"** means (used for introducing a surprising fact) when you think about or remember something. ((किसी आश्‍यचर्जनक तथ्‍य को प्रस्‍तुत करने के लिए प्रयुक्त) (इस बात को) ध्यान में रखते हुए)

questions.question:
**Direction: A sentence has been given with a blank to be filled with an appropriate option. Choose the correct alternative.**

Your presence ______ both my brother and sister.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "affects." **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Affects"** is the correct verb form to use in this sentence, as it is the third person singular present tense form of the verb **"affect." **
 
• **"Affect"** means to have an influence on or cause a change in something or someone. (किसी वस्‍तु या व्‍यक्ति के व्‍यवहार को प्रभावित करना; असर डालना)
 
 
• **Example**: *Her personal problems seem to be **affecting**__ her work.*
 
 
 
• In this sentence, the subject **"your presence"** is the cause of the effect on both the brother and sister.
 
• The verb **"affects" **agrees with the singular subject **"presence."**
 
• The correct answer is Option 4.

 

**Correct sentence**: *Your presence __**affects**__ both my brother and sister.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1, "affecting"**, is a present participle form of the verb and would require a helping verb (such as "is" or "was") to make a complete sentence.
 
• **Option 2, "effect"**, is a noun and means a change that is caused by something; a result. (प्रभाव; परिणाम)

 
 
• **Option 3, "effects",** is the plural form of the noun **"effect"** and does not agree with the singular subject **"presence."**
